main_claim: The unchanged source-selected CpG model reproduces prior predictions. Most selected methylation directions persist in BMI-discordant twin bulk adipose tissue, while discrimination is lower across tissue and endpoint.

a.gene_assignment: native Illumina hg19 gene annotation; retain unassigned explicitly

b.interval: 95% conditional bootstrap intervals; twin-family bootstrap for GSE68336
b.omission: training-set resubstitution remains in comparison table, not plotted as validation

c.type: paired twin CpG effect forest plot
c.selection: BH q < 0.05 across the 50 preselected source-model probes
c.interval: paired-t 95% confidence intervals across 24 twin families

statistical_units.GSE68336: 24 BMI-discordant twin pairs, 48 people; 11 concordant pairs are descriptive only

limitations: GSE68336 has ordinal within-family BMI, not an absolute clinical-obesity diagnosis.
Bulk subcutaneous adipose tissue differs from isolated adipocytes.
Four EPIC CpG effects are unavailable; grey x cells preserve them, and the frozen prediction pipeline uses its pre-existing source-fitted imputation.
Discovery effects are descriptive after source feature selection.
Previous replication cohorts were already inspected; this is independent computational replay.
Gene-body and promoter mappings are annotation associations, not methylation-to-expression causal evidence.
Intervals are conditional on realized predictions, not full model-selection uncertainty.
